intro: Governs wills for people of all religions (except Muslims), and inheritance without a will for Christians, Parsis and those married under the Special Marriage Act. Hindus' inheritance without a will is under the Hindu Succession Act.

sections.p: Any adult of sound mind. A will made while drunk, ill or otherwise unable to understand what one is doing is invalid.
A will, or any part of it, made because of fraud, coercion or undue influence that takes away the person's free will is void.

sections.t: How to make a valid will
sections.p: Must be in writing, signed (or thumb-marked) by the person making it, and attested by at least two witnesses who saw them sign. Witnesses shouldn't be beneficiaries. Registration and stamp paper are not required, though registration helps.
k: Writing the will on plain paper is fine
Name an executor to carry out the will

sections.p: A will can be revoked or changed any time during the person's life — by a new will, a codicil (signed and attested like a will), or by tearing or burning it with intent to revoke. The latest valid will prevails.

Probate (court certification of a will) is required for wills made in, or concerning immovable property within, the old presidency towns — including the Chennai area under the Madras High Court's original jurisdiction. Elsewhere it's optional but can help when banks or authorities ask.

When a Christian (or person under this part) dies without a will: if survived by a spouse and children, the spouse gets one-third and the children share two-thirds equally — sons and daughters alike. With no children, the spouse gets half and relatives the rest.

To collect debts and securities (bank deposits, shares) of a deceased person, heirs can apply to the civil court for a succession certificate. In Tamil Nadu, a legal heir certificate from the Tahsildar is commonly used for government and bank purposes.
